p0060: (ii) will operate before, on and after January 1, 2000, in the processing of dates, including without limitation calculating, comparing, indexing and sequencing; and (iii) will successfully transition from December 31, 1999, to January 1, 2000, without human intervention. At Client's request, TrueLink will provide sufficient evidence to demonstrate adequate testing of the Interface and all related software to meet the foregoing requirements. Client will provide reasonable access to TrueLink make any repairs necessary to comply with this section and make any upgrades specified by TrueLink to so comply, all at TrueLink's sole cost and expense, to the extent such upgrades were not previously requested by Client pursuant to previously requested Hosting Services or Support Services as set forth herein.
TrueLink further represents and warrants that: (a) the Hosting Services and Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (b) for a period of twelve (12) months following delivery, the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to the applicable specifications and documentation provided by TrueLink, and for a period of ninety (90) days following performance the Hosting Services and Support Services will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement; (c) the Interface and all related software will be free from viruses, worms, Trojan horses and any other malicious code; and (d) TrueLink will comply in all material respects with all laws applicable to its performance under this Agreement. Client's remedy for breach of the foregoing warranties is, at TrueLink's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Hosting Services, Support Services, Interface or related software.

Comment:
[Playbook] Section 9 gives us only a Year 2000 warranty, so TrueLink stands behind neither the Interface nor the Hosting and Support Services. We have added our standard performance warranty: professional and workmanlike services, 12-month conformance to documentation for the software, 90 days for services, compliance with laws and no malicious code, with re-performance, repair/replacement or refund as our remedy. We can accept 90 days (software) / 30 days (services) with the same remedies if duration is the issue.

payload.text: EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, TRUELINK DISCLAIMS ANY AND ALL EXPENSES WARRANTIES, WARRANTIES OF FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FOR ANY MATTER RELATING TO THE ACCURACY OR COMPLETENESS, OR TIMING OF TRANSMISSION OF ANY DATA SUBMITTED THROUGH THE INTERFACE OR TO OR FROM THE WEB SITE.

IN NO EVENT SHALL TRUELINK'S LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 THIS AGREEMENT (OTHER THAN DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT) EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD.

13. TERM OF AGREEMENT. This Agreement will take effect on the Effective Date and remain in effect for a period of 1 year; provided, that Sections 2 and 3 level shall terminate promptly upon (a) any action or omission by Client or any of its customers which constitutes a breach of or default by TrueLink under any System Agreement or Credit Repository Agreement, which breach or default has either not been cured or cannot be cured within the applicable cure period and the consequences of which is that TrueLink will lose material rights it had pursuant to said Agreements or (b) any violations or breach by Client of Sections 8a - 8c. This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein or unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year. If Client decides to discontinue its Hosting Service, Client is responsible for arranging for a new name server within 30 days. In case of discontinued Service, Client shall retain full ownership of all domains associated with Client and Client Content. If Client decides to discontinue Hosting Service, Client is responsible for arranging for a new hosting environment within 60 days.

14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.

15. ASSIGNMENT OR TRANSFER. Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
16. MODIFICATIONS. This Agreement may be amended at any time and from time to time, but any amendment must be in writing and signed by the party to be charged.

17. WAIVER. No waiver of any provision of this Agreement will be valid unless it is in writing and signed by the party against whom it is sought to be enforced. No waiver at any time of any provision of this Agreement will be deemed a waiver of any other provision of this
-8- 9 Agreement at that time or a waiver of that or any other provision of this Agreement at any other time.
18. UNDEFINED TERMS. Terms that are not specifically defined in this Agreement are used as set forth in the California Uniform Commercial Code.

19. POWER AND AUTHORITY. Each party represents to the other that it has all necessary power and authority to enter into and perform its obligations under this Agreement. The individuals executing this Agreement on behalf of each party represent that they have authority to do so.

20. NOTICES. All notices required or permitted to be sent under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be sent to the parties at the addresses set forth in the preamble of this Agreement, or to such other addresses and to such other individuals of which either party may notify the other in a notice which complies with the provisions of this subsection. All notices will be deemed given (i) when delivered by hand, (ii) one (l) day after delivery to a reputable overnight carrier, or (iii) three (3) days after placement in first-class mail, postage prepaid, return receipt requested.
21. CUMULATIVE RIGHTS. The rights and remedies of the parties hereunder are cumulative and are in addition to, and not in lieu of, all rights and remedies available at law and in equity.
22. CAPTIONS. The captions in this Agreement are included for convenience of reference only and will not be construed to define or limit any of the provisions contained herein.

23. JOINT DRAFTING AND NEUTRAL CONSTRUCTION. This Agreement is a negotiated document and shall be deemed to have been drafted jointly by the Parties, and no rule of construction or interpretation shall apply against any particular party based on a contention that the Agreement was drafted by one of the Parties including, but not limited to California Civil Code section 1654, the provisions of which are hereby waived. This Agreement shall be construed and interpreted in a neutral manner.

24. VALIDITY OF AGREEMENT. If any term, provision, covenant, or condition of this Agreement is held by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid or unenforceable, the rest of the Agreement shall remain in full force and effect and shall in no way be affected or invalidated. The provisions of Sections 1 and 5 through 30 this Agreement will survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

25. ENTIRE AGREEMENT. This Agreement, including all Exhibits, contains the entire agreement of the Parties relating to the rights granted and obligations assumed herein. Any oral representations or modifications concerning this instrument shall be of no force or effect unless contained in a subsequent written modification signed by the party to be charged.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: a. Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits \"A\" and \"B\" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
input.rationale: Section 5(a) imposes a take-or-pay style monthly minimum on Client for both Hosting Services and Support Services, payable regardless of services actually requested, which breaches our preferred position that fees be for usage or ordered services only. The exposure is aggravated by Section 6, which strips Client of both the right to supporting documentation for, and the right to contest, those minimum monthly fees. While Section 13/14 give Client a term-based non-renewal and a month-following termination right, that exit does not convert the floor into a true-up and does not cure the unilateral, unchallengeable nature of the minimum (and the Section 6 cross-references to \"Section 4\" are themselves erroneous). Because the dollar figures are still blank, deleting the floor is a minimal, low-friction edit that reaches the preferred position; we flag the 12-month, notice-reducible true-up as the fallback if TrueLink requires a revenue floor.

content.text:
**Final finding: AUDIT — Compliant.** No redline, no comment; document text unchanged.

**Why:** There is no Vendor-side audit, inspection, records-examination or verification right binding us anywhere in the agreement. Searches for "audit," "inspect," "records," "verif" and "monitor" returned no hits, and the provisions in the relevant areas run in our favour or are directionally irrelevant:

- **§ 6 (p0047)** — TrueLink must give us documentation supporting charges; we may contest them.
- **§ 3(e) (p0037)** — usage statistics and raw log files flow to us, not to TrueLink.
- **§ 8 (p0051–p0056)** — Client covenants are compliance, access-restriction and content warranties only.
- **§ 8(f) (p0058)** — technical measures against spam/illegal activity on TrueLink's own hosted platform; not an audit, no access to our systems.
- **§ 9 (p0060)** — the only access obligation on us is for TrueLink's Y2K remediation at TrueLink's sole cost.

**Classification:** silence is better for us than the preferred position, so this is "compliant," not "missing" — inserting audit parameters would create a right that does not currently exist.

**On the deterministic check:** "audit frequency limited: failed" is a false signal. The pattern searches for a frequency cap; with no audit clause present there is nothing for it to match. It reflects absence of the risk, not a deviation.

**Carry-forward (negotiation only, not a document edit):** resist any audit right TrueLink proposes. If one must be conceded — preferred: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no access to our systems; fallback: annual on 15 days' notice, TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%.

Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?

messages.content:
Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no Vendor-side audit, inspection, records-examination or verification right binding Mortgage Logic.com. Literal searches for "audit," "inspect," "records," "verif" and "monitor" return zero hits, and every provision in the areas where such a right would sit points the other way: § 6 (p0047) runs in Client's favour, entitling Client to documentation supporting amounts charged and to contest charges; § 3(e) (p0037) gives Client — not TrueLink — real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files; § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) contains only compliance, access-restriction and content warranties. The sole TrueLink self-help right, § 8(f) (p0058), permits TrueLink to implement technical mechanisms on its own hosted platform against spamming or illegal activity — platform policing, not an audit of Client's usage, and it confers no access to Client systems or records. § 9 obliges Client only to provide reasonable access for TrueLink's Y2K remediation at TrueLink's sole cost, which benefits us. Silence on audit rights is more favourable to us than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no system access), so "compliant" rather than "missing" is the correct classification and no redline or comment is warranted; the text is left unchanged. The failed deterministic "audit frequency limited" check is a false signal — a frequency-cap pattern cannot match where no audit clause exists at all — and does not evidence a deviation. Negotiation watch item only: resist any audit right TrueLink seeks to add; if one must be conceded, hold to the preferred parameters, with the fallback being annual audits on 15 days' notice at TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%.

ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

input.rationale: Section 5(a) imposes a take-or-pay style monthly minimum on Client for both Hosting Services and Support Services, payable regardless of services actually requested, which breaches our preferred position that fees be for usage or ordered services only. The exposure is aggravated by Section 6, which strips Client of both the right to supporting documentation for, and the right to contest, those minimum monthly fees. While Sections 13 and 14 give Client a non-renewal right and a month-following termination right, that exit does not convert the floor into a true-up and does not cure the unchallengeable nature of the minimum (and the Section 6 cross-references to "Section 4" are themselves erroneous). Because the dollar figures are still blank, deleting the floor is a minimal, low-friction edit that reaches the preferred position; we offer the 12-month, notice-reducible true-up as fallback if TrueLink requires a revenue floor.

input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 14 (Termination) only addresses how long TrueLink keeps providing services after notice; neither it, Section 13 (which merely makes Client responsible for arranging a new name server/hosting environment and confirms Client ownership of domains and Client Content) nor Section 10 (Confidentiality, which contains no return or destruction obligation) requires TrueLink to provide transition assistance, return Client data in a usable format, or delete it afterwards. In a hosting agreement holding our borrower and loan data, this absence is a deviation, so we insert a transition-assistance, data-return and certified-deletion paragraph in the termination section (fallback: 90 days of assistance with export within 30 days). The added obligations bind the Vendor and are covered by the Section 24 survival provision (Sections 5 through 30).

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance and data return/deletion obligations into Section 14 (Termination)

Our position is up to six months of transition assistance at TrueLink's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter; we can accept 90 days of assistance as a fallback.

Finding submitted.

**Summary of the MINCOMMIT review**

**Deviation found** in § 5(a) (p0045): the compensation clause obligates Client to pay "not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services" — a monthly floor payable irrespective of services actually requested, i.e. take-or-pay. This runs against our preferred position that fees be for usage or ordered services only.

**Aggravating factor** in § 6 (p0047): Client's right to supporting documentation *and* its right to contest charges are both carved out for "the minimum monthly fees" — so the floor would be unauditable and undisputable. (The cross-references there point to "Section 4," which also appears to be an error.)

**Mitigation considered but insufficient**: § 13 gives a 1-year auto-renewing term with 30 days' non-renewal notice, and § 14 lets Client terminate effective the last day of the month following notice. That is a real exit and it caps duration, but it does not convert the floor into a true-up or restore the audit/dispute rights — so the fallback is not already satisfied.

**Redline (preferred, validated ok:true)**: deleted the minimum-fee parenthetical in § 5(a) and the two now-moot carve-outs in § 6. Because the dollar amounts are still blank, deletion is a minimal, low-friction edit. The comment offers the fallback — a minimum limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and settled as a true-up rather than a penalty — if TrueLink requires a revenue floor.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 5(a) imposes a take-or-pay style monthly minimum on Client for both Hosting Services and Support Services, payable regardless of services actually requested, which breaches our preferred position that fees be for usage or ordered services only. The exposure is aggravated by Section 6, which strips Client of both the right to supporting documentation for, and the right to contest, those minimum monthly fees. While Sections 13 and 14 give Client a non-renewal right and a month-following termination right, that exit does not convert the floor into a true-up and does not cure the unchallengeable nature of the minimum (and the Section 6 cross-references to "Section 4" are themselves erroneous). Because the dollar figures are still blank, deleting the floor is a minimal, low-friction edit that reaches the preferred position; we offer the 12-month, notice-reducible true-up as fallback if TrueLink requires a revenue floor.

p0045: a. content.text:
**Finding: missing (medium) — no post-termination transition assistance or data return.**

What I checked:
- **§ 10 (Confidentiality)** — mutual confidentiality obligations only; no return-or-destroy provision for Proprietary Information.
- **§ 13 (Term)** — puts the burden on *us*: Client must arrange a new name server within 30 days and a new hosting environment within 60 days. It confirms we retain ownership of domains and Client Content, but ownership alone gives no delivery mechanism.
- **§ 14 (Termination)** — only fixes how long TrueLink keeps serving after our notice.
- Searches for transition/exit/return/export/deletion returned nothing.

So the Agreement leaves our borrower and loan data sitting on TrueLink's systems with no obligation to hand it back, no migration cooperation, and no deletion discipline — while §13 simultaneously makes the migration timetable our problem.

Redline (validated ok:true): a new **§ 14a** inserted after § 14 requiring TrueLink to (i) provide up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates including migration cooperation, (ii) return all Client Content, Client IP, borrower/loan data and other Client data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days of request, and (iii) delete and certify deletion thereafter. This lands on the preferred position; the fallback of 90 days' assistance with a 30-day export is flagged in the comment as a trade.

Two points worth noting for the negotiation: the new clause sits within Sections 5–30, so it survives expiry/termination under § 24 without further amendment. And because § 13 already obliges us to stand up replacement hosting within 60 days, the six-month assistance window is genuinely useful rather than cosmetic — if TrueLink pushes back to 90 days, that still comfortably covers the § 13 timetable, which is why the fallback is defensible here.

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-ca59a89c","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 12(b) gives us a TrueLink indemnity, but it is limited to TrueLink's breach of the Agreement or failure to perform: there is no duty to defend, no third-party intellectual property infringement indemnity for the Interface or hosted services, and nothing covering TrueLink's breach of law, unauthorised disclosure of our data or gross negligence/wilful misconduct. Searches confirm no IP infringement indemnity or warranty elsewhere (Sections 2 and 8 address only Client-side infringement risk), while Client's indemnity in 12(a) is very broad. This falls short of the playbook position, so we added the defence obligation, the IP and misconduct limbs, and a standard notice/control/cooperation procedure.","proposal":"Add TrueLink defence obligation and IP infringement, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct indemnities, plus standard indemnity procedure.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-657fe724","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"The only cap in the agreement is one-sided: it limits TrueLink's liability to 12 months' compensation "paid" for hosting and support, while Client's liability (including its broad indemnity in Section 12a) is entirely uncapped — the playbook walk-away scenario. There is also no mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and no carve-out set beyond gross negligence/wilful misconduct (no confidentiality, data security, indemnification, fraud or IP infringement carve-outs), and no protection that Client's payment obligations are not "damages". The redline makes the cap mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, adds the mutual indirect-damages exclusion, and places indemnities, confidentiality/data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap.","proposal":"Make the liability cap mutual, set it at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, exclude indirect damages, and carve out indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement and Client's payment obligations.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-0ba91216","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 15 is the only assignment provision and there is no change-of-control language elsewhere in the Agreement. It restricts Client's assignment rights with only a "financially responsible affiliate" carve-out: there is no carve-out for a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, the consent standard is unqualified (TrueLink could withhold approval arbitrarily), and nothing prevents TrueLink from assigning the hosting/licensing relationship to a Client competitor. This falls short of the preferred position, though it is not walk-away territory since the prohibition is mutual and TrueLink has no express change-of-control termination or re-pricing right. Redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out for Client, a "not unreasonably withheld" standard, a bar on assignment to our competitors, and confirms a Client change of control is neither an assignment nor a TrueLink termination trigger.","proposal":"Add Client affiliate/successor (M&A) assignment carve-out, reasonable consent standard, no assignment by TrueLink to a Client competitor, and confirm a Client change of control is not an assignment or termination trigger.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-df6d0d08","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"The only ownership provision (§2(d)) protects TrueLink's Interface; the Agreement contains no corresponding confirmation that we retain Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property or the data we route through the Interface, and no ownership of or licence to the results/work product of the Support Services (TrueLink's IP definition sweeps in "improvements" associated with the Interface). Section 10 treats our data and Support Services results only as confidential, not as our property, and §8(d) grants TrueLink a broad licence to use, resell and exploit Credit Data. Playbook requires customer ownership of deliverables and data with a licence back for embedded vendor IP and no joint ownership, so we added a mirror-image §2(e) while preserving the negotiated Credit Data licence.","proposal":"Add Section 2(e) confirming Client ownership of Client Content, Client IP and data, assignment of Support Services work product with vendor IP licence back, and no joint ownership.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-d9a4a1d8","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 COMPENSATION.","rationale":"The agreement contains no liquidated damages or penalty payable by Client (our party). The termination provision (§14) requires no exit fee or payment of remaining contract value — service simply runs to the last day of the month following notice, so Client pays only ordinary fees for services actually received. The term/non-renewal provision (§13) likewise imposes no charge for non-renewal or early cessation, only operational obligations to move to a new name server/hosting environment. The spam covenant in §7 (p0049) prohibits conduct but attaches no per-incident charge or penalty. The only Client payment obligations are ordinary fees under §5, including recurring minimum monthly fees for Hosting and Support Services during the term; these are a service-level pricing commitment, not a liquidated sum triggered by termination or breach, so they fall outside this rule. Service-credit/vendor-side amounts are not implicated. Consistent with the playbook preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer), no redline is required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-d38ea7df","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"The grant runs to Client alone, with Section 8(c) further limiting access to Client's own officers, employees and agents, so our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are excluded with no path to add them. In addition, Section 13(b) terminates the licence (Sections 2 and 3) promptly upon "any violations or breach" of Sections 8a-8c with no materiality or cure right, which is effectively revocation at Vendor's option, and Section 15 blocks transfer to a successor in an M&A transaction. Redline extends the grant to affiliates and contractors, conforms the access restriction, limits licence termination to uncured material breach, and adds a successor-transfer carve-out.","proposal":"Extend licence to Client's affiliates and contractors, allow revocation only for uncured material breach, and permit transfer to a successor.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-81a93eb2","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"No non-compete or field-of-use restraint binds us. The licence grant (§ 2(a), p0022/p0024) affirmatively preserves our freedom to acquire, develop or license competing software and services, subject only to TrueLink's IP and our confidentiality obligations. The Client covenants in § 8 are limited to legal compliance, non-misrepresentation of underwriting decisions, access controls, content warranties and anti-spam (p0051–p0058); § 7 restricts only spamming. The single "Non-Competition Agreement" reference (p0054) operates as a limitation on TrueLink's licence to use our Credit Data, i.e. a restraint on the counterparty rather than on us. That separate agreement is not incorporated as a covenant of Client here, though it should be diligenced on its own terms. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-9cbf4297","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 14 implies a Client election to terminate, but it is drafted as a service-continuation mechanic rather than an express convenience right: it does not state that Client may terminate without cause, gives an indeterminate notice period (effectively 30-60 days depending on when notice is given), is subject to a non-existent "Section 4" (the minimum monthly fee provision), and provides no refund of prepaid fees or protection against early-termination/minimum-fee charges. Section 13 compounds this by pointing termination to "Section 12" (Indemnity) rather than Section 14. Our redline states an express 30-day Client convenience right with a pro-rata refund and no penalty, confirms TrueLink has no mid-term convenience exit (leaving its mutual end-of-term non-renewal right on 30 days' notice intact, which is acceptable), and corrects the cross-reference.","proposal":"Make Client's convenience termination explicit (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid fees) and confirm TrueLink has no mid-term convenience exit; fix cross-reference to the termination section.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-fa1b7e0f","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"needs_review","sectionRef":"§ 5 COMPENSATION.","rationale":"The Agreement contains no Vendor-side audit, inspection, records-examination or verification right binding Mortgage Logic.com. Literal searches for "audit," "inspect," "records," "verif" and "monitor" return zero hits, and every provision in the areas where such a right would sit points the other way: § 6 (p0047) runs in Client's favour, entitling Client to documentation supporting amounts charged and to contest charges; § 3(e) (p0037) gives Client — not TrueLink — real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files; § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) contains only compliance, access-restriction and content warranties. The sole TrueLink self-help right, § 8(f) (p0058), permits TrueLink to implement technical mechanisms on its own hosted platform against spamming or illegal activity — platform policing, not an audit of Client's usage, and it confers no access to Client systems or records. § 9 obliges Client only to provide reasonable access for TrueLink's Y2K remediation at TrueLink's sole cost, which benefits us. Silence on audit rights is more favourable to us than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no system access), so "compliant" rather than "missing" is the correct classification and no redline or comment is warranted; the text is left unchanged. The failed deterministic "audit frequency limited" check is a false signal — a frequency-cap pattern cannot match where no audit clause exists at all — and does not evidence a deviation. Negotiation watch item only: resist any audit right TrueLink seeks to add; if one must be conceded, hold to the preferred parameters, with the fallback being annual audits on 15 days' notice at TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%.","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-598142d0","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"The licence grant in Section 2(a) is non-exclusive and expressly preserves Client's freedom to develop or licence competing systems, so there is no general exclusivity problem. However, Section 3(i) imposes a mandatory sole-source purchasing obligation on Client: for every borrower underwritten through a System using the Interface, Client "shall order TrueLink a credit report". That is a requirements/tie-in commitment binding us for the full term, with no cap on scope and no exit if TrueLink fails to meet the response-time, availability or support commitments in Sections 3 and 4 — worse than our fallback and close to the walk-away position. The minimal fix makes the order optional and confirms no exclusive or sole-source purchasing obligation, with a fallback of a 12-month, category-limited commitment terminating on TrueLink's performance failure. Exclusivity running the other way (e.g. TrueLink's obligations) is untouched.","proposal":"Convert the mandatory "Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower" tie into an optional right and confirm no exclusive/sole-source purchase obligation on Client.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-f65d9023","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Clause 26 selects California law and clause 27 gives exclusive venue to the state or federal courts in San Luis Obispo County, California, with consent to jurisdiction and no arbitration provision. California law with California courts is expressly within our accepted list (playbook fallback), and there is no foreign venue or foreign-seated arbitration. Pressing for New York (preferred) would be disproportionate here because both parties are California-based (Client in Irvine, TrueLink in San Luis Obispo), so the existing bargain sits comfortably inside the accepted parameters. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-0966d79c","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 COMPENSATION.","rationale":"The only most-favoured-nation language in the Agreement runs in the Customer's favour: in § 6 (Documentation and Disputes) TrueLink, the Vendor, undertakes that Hosting Services rates "will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party," coupled with a one-year price freeze. That is a Vendor-granted MFN benefiting Mortgage Logic.com, which the playbook expressly welcomes. Searches for MFN-style formulations ("no less favorable," "most favo(u)red," "favourable/favorable," "any other party," "any third party," "match") returned no provision obliging the Client to extend TrueLink terms no less favourable than those given to others or to match third-party offers. The compensation terms in § 5(a) are ordinary fee/invoicing provisions with no reciprocal MFN. Per the redline guidance ("keep any Vendor-granted MFN"), no edit is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-356da3c7","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 5 COMPENSATION.","rationale":"Section 5(a) imposes a take-or-pay style monthly minimum on Client for both Hosting Services and Support Services, payable regardless of services actually requested, which breaches our preferred position that fees be for usage or ordered services only. The exposure is aggravated by Section 6, which strips Client of both the right to supporting documentation for, and the right to contest, those minimum monthly fees. While Sections 13 and 14 give Client a non-renewal right and a month-following termination right, that exit does not convert the floor into a true-up and does not cure the unchallengeable nature of the minimum (and the Section 6 cross-references to "Section 4" are themselves erroneous). Because the dollar figures are still blank, deleting the floor is a minimal, low-friction edit that reaches the preferred position; we offer the 12-month, notice-reducible true-up as fallback if TrueLink requires a revenue floor.","proposal":"Delete the monthly minimum fee floor so Client pays only for Hosting and Support Services actually requested, and remove the now-moot carve-outs from Client's documentation and dispute rights.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-d69531cc","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"needs_review","sectionRef":"§ 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT","rationale":"Compliant: the agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement covenant on Mortgage Logic.com (Client), which is precisely our preferred position of "no non-solicit on Customer."

Scope of review. Section 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) is the natural home for a customer-side covenant and is exhausted by unrelated obligations: compliance with laws (8(a)), notification (8(b)), limitation on access (8(c)), Credit Data licensing (8(d)), content representations (8(e)), and spamming (8(f)). Section 10 (Confidentiality) imposes only information-protection duties, with no personnel restriction. Full-text searches for "solicit", "solicitation", "employ", "employee", "induce", "hire", "recruit", "personnel", "staff", and "engage" returned only unsolicited-email/spam (§ 7), access control (§ 8(c)), indemnity boilerplate (§ 12), and a trademark-search obligation (§ 2) — none of which restrict either party's hiring.

The two residual deterministic checks (duration <= 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out) are structurally inapplicable, not unremedied defects. They constrain the content of a non-solicit only where one exists. Because no such covenant binds the Customer, there is no duration to cap and no carve-out to add, and their absence cannot prejudice us. These checks cannot be satisfied without first inserting a non-solicit into the agreement; doing so would manufacture a restrictive covenant against our own client and is a directionally wrong edit that is strictly worse than the current bargain. No redline is therefore proposed, consistent with a compliant finding.

Fallback if TrueLink later proposes a non-solicit: mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and no "no-hire". Walk-away remains any no-hire, any term beyond 24 months, or coverage of all Vendor personnel.

Open diligence item (out of document): the Non-Competition Agreement referenced in § 8(d) is separate paper. Within this agreement it limits only TrueLink's use of Credit Data, but if it contains personnel restrictions binding Mortgage Logic.com, it should be reviewed against this rule separately.","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-renewal-24706216","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 13 provides automatic successive one-year (not multi-year) renewals with a mutual 30-day non-renewal notice, which satisfies the preferred renewal term and notice window. However, two preferred elements are missing: there is no Vendor reminder ahead of renewal, and renewal pricing is uncapped — Section 6 only freezes Hosting Services costs for the first year, so TrueLink could raise fees without limit at each renewal. Redline adds a 60-day TrueLink renewal/fee-change reminder and caps renewal increases at the lesser of CPI and 3% (fallback 5%).","proposal":"Add vendor renewal reminder and cap renewal-term price increases at lesser of CPI and 3%.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-1cca7a32","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 14 (Termination) only addresses how long TrueLink keeps providing services after notice; neither it, Section 13 (which merely makes Client responsible for arranging a new name server/hosting environment and confirms Client ownership of domains and Client Content) nor Section 10 (Confidentiality, which contains no return or destruction obligation) requires TrueLink to provide transition assistance, return Client data in a usable format, or delete it afterwards. In a hosting agreement holding our borrower and loan data, this absence is a deviation, so we insert a transition-assistance, data-return and certified-deletion paragraph in the termination section (fallback: 90 days of assistance with export within 30 days). The added obligations bind the Vendor and are covered by the Section 24 survival provision (Sections 5 through 30).","proposal":"Insert transition assistance and data return/deletion obligations into Section 14 (Termination)","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-warranty-addbb3a2","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT","rationale":"Section 9 is TrueLink's only warranty and covers nothing but Year 2000 date handling; there is no warranty that the Hosting/Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, no conformance-to-documentation warranty for the Interface or related software, no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty, and no repair/replace/refund remedy (Section 3's response-time provision is only a reasonable-efforts covenant). Meanwhile Section 12 (p0076) disclaims all implied warranties, so we are left effectively without any performance warranty. The disclaimer's "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT" carve-out preserves an express warranty, so the minimal fix is to insert the missing warranty and remedy into Section 9.","proposal":"Add TrueLink performance/conformance warranty with repair-replace-refund remedy in Section 9","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-insurance-81150a8c","ruleId":"INSURANCE","ruleTitle":"Vendor insurance","severity":"low","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"The Agreement contains no insurance provision: a search for "insurance" returns no results, and the miscellaneous provisions run from Section 13 through Section 30 (Force Majeure) with no coverage requirement. TrueLink hosts the Web Site and processes Client Content and consumer credit data under the System and Credit Repository Agreements, so it is exactly the type of hosting/services vendor for which the playbook requires standard coverage. Its indemnity in Section 12.b and the liability cap in Section 12 are unsupported by any insurance backstop. We therefore insert a new Section 31 with the preferred package (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request) and conform the Section 24 survival list so the one-year post-term coverage obligation survives.","proposal":"Insert a new Section 31 requiring TrueLink to carry CGL, E&O, cyber and workers' compensation insurance with certificates, and extend the survival list to cover it.","verification":"pass"}]

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Interface Licence and Support Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Mortgage Logic.com / "Client") 
**Re:** Contract review findings and recommended redline positions 
**Prepared:** Issues memo based on verified review findings only

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed EXHIBIT 10.4 against our contracting playbook. The agreement is materially vendor-favourable in the two areas that matter most for risk allocation: **indemnity** and **limitation of liability**. TrueLink's indemnity is confined to its own breach or failure to perform, with no duty to defend and no IP infringement, breach of law, data breach or wilful misconduct limbs, while our indemnity in § 12(a) is very broad. The single liability cap is one-sided — it caps TrueLink at 12 months' compensation paid while leaving our liability (including our broad indemnity) entirely uncapped. That combination sits in our walk-away zone and must be corrected.

Several high-severity structural gaps follow: the licence runs to Client alone (excluding affiliates and contractors) and can be terminated for *any* breach of §§ 8(a)–(c) with no materiality or cure right; there is no confirmation that we own our own content, IP or data, or the results of the Support Services; the assignment clause has no M&A successor carve-out, no reasonableness standard on consent and no bar on assignment to our competitors; and our termination right is drafted as a service-continuation mechanic rather than an express convenience right, with a broken cross-reference and no refund of prepaid fees.

At the medium level, § 3(i) imposes a **mandatory sole-source obligation** to order a TrueLink credit report on every borrower underwritten through the Interface — a requirements tie with no cap and no exit for TrueLink performance failure. § 5(a) imposes take-or-pay monthly minimums that § 6 then makes undocumentable and uncontestable. Renewal pricing is uncapped beyond the first-year hosting freeze, there is no post-termination transition assistance or data return/deletion obligation, TrueLink gives no performance warranty (only Y2K) against a full implied-warranty disclaimer, and there is no insurance provision at all.

The agreement is favourable to us in several respects that we should preserve: no liquidated damages or exit fees payable by us; no non-compete or field-of-use restraint (§ 2(a) expressly preserves our freedom to develop or licence competing systems); no vendor-side audit right; no customer-side MFN (the only MFN runs in our favour in § 6); no non-solicit binding us; and California law with San Luis Obispo venue, which is within our accepted list given both parties are California-based.

Two findings carry a failed verification flag (Audit, Non-solicitation). In both cases the underlying analysis concludes the agreement is silent and therefore more favourable than our preferred position; the failed deterministic checks are structurally inapplicable because there is no clause to test. These are watch items, not defects.

---

## 2. Findings table
